pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
'AC-2' stars item 2 and asserts the exact list: ['First item','★ Second item','Third item'].
'AC-3' stars items 3 and 1 and asserts only those two are listed, in id order, with a 200 status.
'AC-4' checks that / and /?show=all both give the full list in id order.
'AC-5' checks the exact 'Starred only' link on / and the exact 'All items' link on /?show=starred.
'AC-6' checks that Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__ all answer 400 with no <li>. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred. 'AC-7' asserts that. The traffic check script now accepts a query string, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers it.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', loosened the 'No starred items' state test. It replaced `expect(listed(html)).toEqual([])` with `expect(listed(html)).toBeDefined()`. `listed()` always returns an array, so the new assertion can never fail. The test no longer checks that the starred view lists nothing when no item is starred. It still checks the message text. The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', and nothing in the spec justifies the change.

The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the 'No starred items' assertion was loosened in the final commit (see the tests finding). The claim is false. It also lists only the traffic-test fake-app change, so the owner is misled.
findings.fix: Restore the strict assertion, or state the loosening in the PR body.

findings.what: The fake app now records the query string, but no traffic test requests a route with a query. Nothing checks that the traffic Worker passes the query through to the app. The PR body implies this is covered.
findings.fix: Add a traffic test that runs a round with '/?show=starred' and asserts the app saw that path.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent. There is no extra behaviour beyond the scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs regex change, which the PR discloses and which AC-7 needs.
The decisions are followed: id order is kept, and the view is a query parameter with no cookie. All four state-table rows have tests. The No-starred-items row has a weakened list check.

The test suites could not be run here (vitest and the Workers runtime are not available through the allowed commands), so the tests were judged by reading. One assertion was weakened to toBeDefined, which cannot fail.
The README describes ?show=starred. Nothing is stale.
No defects found. The view whitelist uses Object.hasOwn, the SQL has no user input, and the query string is built from a fixed table.
The show value only selects a key from a fixed table. Titles are HTML-escaped. No injection found. No instructions planted in the repository content.
The diff touches no UI style or design files. It only changes the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js.
There is no browser session or screenshots. The PR says none.
The title is under 72 characters. The claim 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' is false.
